concepts.title: Magnetic Effect of Electric Current
concepts.definition: An electric current flowing through a wire turns it into a magnet-like region: a compass needle near the wire deflects, and a current-carrying coil picks up iron pins, showing that electricity and magnetism are linked.
concepts.key_idea: Current makes magnetism: deflection of a compass near a wire is the classic evidence.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu104.txt lines 44-140 (current has a magnetic effect)
question_patterns: what happens to a compass needle placed near a current-carrying wire
how can you show that an electric current has a magnetic effect
why does a current-carrying coil attract iron pins
who discovered the magnetic effect of current
what happens to the deflection when the current is switched off
design an activity to demonstrate the magnetic effect of electricity

solution_steps.explain: Connect a wire to a battery through a switch with a compass nearby.
The needle deflects only while current flows, proving the magnetic effect.
The energised coil lifts iron objects, confirming magnet-like behaviour.

concepts.title: Electromagnets
concepts.definition: A coil of wire wound around an iron core becomes an electromagnet when current passes: it acts like a permanent magnet with north and south poles while energised, and its strength grows with more turns, larger current or a soft-iron core.
concepts.key_idea: An electromagnet is a switchable magnet - on with current, off without it.
question_patterns: how is an electromagnet made
why is an iron core used in an electromagnet
how can the strength of an electromagnet be increased
does an electromagnet have poles - explain
how does an electromagnet differ from a bar magnet
name two devices that use electromagnets

solution_steps.explain: Insulated wire is wound closely around an iron nail or core.
Connecting the ends to a battery magnetises the core.
The ends show north and south behaviour, and more turns or current lifts heavier pins.

concepts.title: Heating Effect of Electric Current
concepts.definition: A current-carrying wire warms up because flowing charge loses energy as heat in the conductor; this heating effect is put to work in appliances like the electric heater, iron and bulb filament, and is guarded against in wiring through fuses.
concepts.key_idea: Every current warms its wire - useful in heaters, dangerous in cables.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu104.txt lines 319-459 (does a current-carrying wire get hot)
question_patterns: why does a current-carrying wire become hot

what is the role of a fuse in a household circuit
why does a bulb filament glow
design an activity to show the heating effect of electric current

solution_steps.explain: Connect a resistance wire in a simple circuit.
The wire heats after some time, showing energy turning into heat.
Heaters exploit the effect; fuses melt to cut off excess heating.

concepts.title: How a Battery Generates Electricity
concepts.definition: A battery pushes current through chemical action inside: two different electrodes dipped in an electrolyte react, separating charges and maintaining a potential difference that drives current in the external circuit until the chemicals are used up.
concepts.key_idea: Chemical energy inside the cell becomes electrical energy outside.
concepts.textbook_ref: hecu104.txt lines 459-560 (how does a battery generate electricity)
question_patterns: how does a battery produce electric current
what is the role of the electrolyte in a cell

distinguish a cell from a battery
what energy change happens inside a battery

solution_steps.explain: Two electrodes of different materials sit in an electrolyte paste or liquid.
Reactions separate charges and set up a potential difference between terminals.
The stored chemical energy drives current until reactants run out.
